speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation and have a yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes. To understand the cause of these symptoms, have you been feeling unusually tired, losing your appetite, or experiencing nausea lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis (likely due to Hepatitis A/B/C or drug-induced injury).

The patient's history of high-risk sexual behavior and substance use, combined with recent jaundice and agitation, strongly suggests an acute infectious or toxic hepatitis. Given the "previously healthy" status and specific risk factors, I suspect Hepatitis A or B, or potentially Acetaminophen toxicity. We need to confirm this immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Panel (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase, PT/INR), Viral Hepatitis Panel (Hep A IgM, Hep B surface Ag, Hep C Ab).
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.
